header.reason: Martin, the CFO, saw only a rate comparison and nothing showing what failed orders cost Fernbrook. Sam blames price, but we never put a Fernbrook figure in front of Martin.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Lead with big orders failing at checkout, not average approval uplift.

line.text: Authorization Boost increases acceptance rates by 3.8% on average

findings.why: Lucy came to us because one in twelve online orders failed, and big baskets failed most.
findings.quote: about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Tell the CFO what failed orders cost, right beside our rate.
findings.why: Sam never met Martin, the CFO, who saw both offers as the same and judged on price.
findings.quote: he's not going to pay more for the same thing

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Say what a lower rate leaves unfixed: big orders still failing.
findings.why: Lucy told Sam the bank only cut its rate, and her questions then switched to rate only.
findings.quote: After the bank came back, every email was the rate.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Swap the average uplift claim for why big orders get declined.

line.text: Authorization Boost increases acceptance rates by 3.8% on average

findings.why: Lucy nodded through Farah's big-order explanation, but only our quote reached Martin's page.

findings.finding: Add a one-page case pricing failed orders in the customer's own numbers.

findings.quote: something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.
